title: Minimax Rates and Honest Intervals for Random-Slope Functionals in Binary-Logit Dose Panels
banked_reason: under the bar; no bounded fix in scope
gap_reasons: The note does not deliver the advertised complete joint frontier: it proves root-n sufficiency under polynomial growth of lambda and impossibility when lambda=o(log n), but leaves every intervening array without a necessary-and-sufficient classification.
The claimed uniform Chebyshev block lower bound (1) is not derived.
paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a substantial partial spine: exponential identification geometry, bounded-information minimax and honest-length bounds, exact consistency results, fixed-order Richardson improvements, and a certified finite score construction. The field-level program collapsed because the exact strong-information/root-n transition remains open and the uniform approximation lower bound lacks quantitative control through pole/branch cancellation regimes. A revival must supply growing-order modulus control or another upper construction with matching least-favorable laws, plus a dedicated uniform singularity lemma; dependency and comparison-scope repairs alone cannot lift the tier.
tldr: For binary-logit panels with equal dose-zero and dose-\(c\) blocks under one fixed ceiling \(0<c\le c_0<1\), the proved partial spine gives exponentially shrinking identification ambiguity, a logarithmic weak-information frontier, an if-and-only-if characterization of vanishing minimax RMSE and uniformly honest expected length, and continuum-certified score computation. Fixed-order Richardson correction proves root-\(n\) behavior whenever \(\lambda=mc^2\) has a fixed polynomial lower growth rate, while moment-matched alternatives rule it out when \(\lambda=o(\log n)\). The exact root-\(n\) classification for arrays covered by neither condition remains open, including regular subpolynomial arrays above the logarithmic lower exclusion; no growing-order Richardson claim is made. Proved examples show that the average response can be consistently recovered even when individual slopes cannot. The excluded point \(c=1\) is only a direct-observation reference.
gap: The closest paper proves that average recovery can survive failure of individual recovery and constructs a c_T=T^{-1/2} estimator, but it does not establish necessary joint sample-size conditions, minimax lower bounds, honest expected-length rates, a sharp support-adapted identification diameter, or the diverging-information root-n boundary over a fixed strictly subunit dose class.
fill: First prove or falsify the c-uniform analytic upper and lower approximation lemma, including c=e^{-T}; next validate the fixed-intercept common-baseline chi-square construction; then prove the support-adapted score variance bound. Only after those gates seek the bounded-lambda K_eff frontier, the consistency equivalence, the diverging-information modulus, and the comparison with one-person slope recovery.
